title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations
layout_note: A symmetric V-then-columns diagram: one input circle x at the bottom centre sends two diagonal arrows (labelled t ~ T and t' ~ T) up to two view circles; each rises vertically through h (after f(.)) to z (after g(.)); a horizontal double arrow 'Maximize agreement' joins z_i and z_j at the top and a lighter one 'Representation' sits between h_i and h_j.
grouping: No boxes, containers or colour. Grouping is by symmetry alone: two mirror columns of math symbols, with the functions f(.) and g(.) written as arrow labels on the outer side of each column.
shapes_depth: Pure black line art: inputs and views are outlined circles with bold italic math (x, x~_i, x~_j); intermediates h and z are bare bold symbols with no shape; all operations are thin black arrows carrying their function name as a label. No fills, no shading.
proposed_highlight: Nothing is coloured or boxed; the objective is stated as text on a horizontal double arrow at the top ('Maximize agreement'), and the representation used downstream is marked by a second labelled double arrow between the h's, one level below.
lesson: A whole framework can be drawn as a math diagram: circles for data, bare symbols for intermediates, functions as arrow labels, and the objective as a labelled double arrow across the top — enough when the method has few parts.
notes: Venue from the first page ('Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning, Vienna, Austria, PMLR 119, 2020').

arrangement.units: One unframed diagram: two mirror columns of symbols above a shared input circle.
arrangement.inputs_as: an outlined circle with the symbol x (no image), and two outlined view circles reached by arrows labelled with sampled augmentations t ~ T, t' ~ T
arrangement.losses_at: top, as a horizontal double arrow labelled 'Maximize agreement' between z_i and z_j
arrangement.shared: the shared encoder f(.) and head g(.) appear only as identical arrow labels in both columns

core.what: one input x at the bottom forks into two mirror columns (view -> h -> z) that face each other, with a horizontal double arrow 'Maximize agreement' between z_i and z_j at the top

relations.form: the two columns are mirror images and the objective is a horizontal double arrow spanning the gap between their top symbols z_i and z_j
the encoder f(.) and head g(.) appear only as identical arrow labels in both columns, implying shared weights without drawing them
each column reads bottom to top: augmented view circle, f(.) arrow, h, g(.) arrow, z
two diagonal arrows labelled t ~ T and t' ~ T leave the input circle to the two view circles, showing two independent augmentations

channels.colour: none: the figure is monochrome black on white
channels.shape: outlined circles = data (x and its two views); bare bold symbols = representations h and z; modules exist only as arrow labels
channels.line: single-headed arrows = transformations, labelled with the function or the sampled augmentation; double-headed horizontal arrows are used both for the objective ('Maximize agreement') and for an annotation ('Representation', marking which level is kept), so one line style carries two meanings

quality.strengths: The compared representations z_i and z_j are drawn and face each other across the objective, so what is compared is visible as geometry; h is drawn and marked as the kept representation, separating the trained-on level from the used level; all paths are short and straight.
quality.weaknesses: No image or augmented sample is drawn, so 'views' are abstract circles; the shared encoder is never drawn as one module, only implied by repeated labels; the same double-arrow style means both 'loss' and 'this is the representation'.

insights.structure: One input circle at the bottom centre forks into two mirror columns of symbols (view circle -> h -> z), joined horizontally at two levels by labelled double arrows.
insights.data: Data and features are math only: outlined circles for x and its two views, bare bold symbols for h and z, with no image or tensor drawn.
insights.emphasis: The two horizontal double arrows carry the message as words: 'Maximize agreement' across the top between z's and 'Representation' between the h's, marking what is trained and what is kept.
insights.flow: Bottom-to-top: diagonal arrows labelled with the sampled augmentations climb from x to the views, then straight vertical arrows labelled f(.) and g(.) rise in each column.
insights.avoid: With no boxes or tint, f and g read as edge labels rather than networks, so a reader cannot see that the two columns share weights; a richer method would need explicit modules.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
